why: Drawing marks an applied patch pocket sitting on top of the vest front; photo shows a genuine contrast-fabric patch pocket topstitched onto the surface (not a welt/jetted opening), matching the construction. Only deviation is the patch bottom, drawn flat with rounded corners but photographed with a V-point hem.

Drawing shows a solid-filled horizontal contrast band across the pocket position, i.e. the pocket welt surface itself rendered in contrast cloth; photo shows exactly one horizontal red welt/jetted strip of contrast fabric, edge-stitched, on a black vest at the same waist-level pocket position.

Drawing distinguishes this option by outlining the welt in contrast only at its border while the welt body stays neutral - contrast piping on the pocket seam. The photo is an entirely monochrome navy vest whose two welt pockets are the identical self fabric with no contrast piping, trim, or edge on the seam at all, so the defining contrast element of this contrast-pocket option is absent.

Drawing is a notch-lapel vest with clean unbroken outlines on lapel, front edge and hem plus two welt pockets and four buttons over a bottom buttonhole; the photo reproduces the same notch-lapel five-position front with completely smooth, unstitched lapel and front edges, confirming no pick stitching.

Drawing puts a fine dashed line running parallel to and slightly inset from the V-neck opening, front placket edge and hem point; the photo shows visible hand pick stitching set a few millimetres in from the front edge, tracking the same V-neck and down-front path, which is the 0.6 cm pick stitch being specified.

Drawing is a side-elevation of a single dome-profile fabric-covered button sitting on a small shank; the photo is the same side-on macro of one dome button wrapped in satin cloth with the wrap grain visible and a thread shank underneath, same silhouette and viewpoint.

Drawing magnifies the end of a vest welt pocket to show the opening terminating with no dense sealing/bar stitch across it; the photo jetted vest pocket ends are clean, with the welt corners closing without any bar tack or seal stitch, matching the negative feature being called out.

Drawing highlights the slanted front trouser pocket opening as the stitched zone; the photo shows that same slanted side pocket carrying two parallel rows of topstitching, one riding right on the folded edge and a second set noticeably further in, matching the 0.1 + 0.7 cm double topstitch spec.

Drawing highlights a pointed sharp-cut waistband extension tab carrying a buttonhole, plus a separate hook and bar marked on the waistband. The photo shows the same angled sharp-tipped extension with its buttonhole, a metal hook bar seated on the left waistband and a four-hole button on the right, so all three called-out elements are present.

Drawing marks exactly one pleat line per front panel with the magnified callout showing the fold turning toward the fly; the photo shows one pleat per leg, correct count, with each pleat open wedge flaring toward the centre fly rather than outward toward the side pocket, consistent with a forward pleat.

Drawing shows the fly laid open with a beaded coil running the full vertical length of the fly opening rather than a button placket; the photo shows the fly opened to reveal a fine continuous coil zipper tape down the fly, no fly buttons, which is the nylon coil zip fly.

Drawing is a tall narrow vertical front pocket opening with the magnifier showing a single horizontal I-shape bar tack closing the lower end; the photo shows the same vertical pocket opening with one dense horizontal bar tack stitched squarely across the bottom of the opening, same shape, count and location.
